Once the 2D Euler loop on [Gierer-Meinhardt Solver in 2D](gierer-meinhardt-2d-solver.qmd) passes the time-step check, you can look at the field. Plot one static snapshot first. Animate only after the snapshot looks right, as in [Animation in 1D](gierer-meinhardt-1d-animation.qmd).

## Plot a Snapshot

`imshow` draws the matrix `uv[1]`. Rows are $x$ and columns are $y$, so the horizontal axis of the image is $y$.

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
im = ax.imshow(
    uv[1],
    interpolation="bilinear",
    origin="lower",
    extent=[0, length_y, 0, length_x],
)
ax.set_xlabel("y")
ax.set_ylabel("x")
plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label="v(x, y)")
plt.show()
```

## Animate the Simulation

Run this code as a Python script, not in a notebook, so the animation window updates smoothly.

::: {.callout-note}
## Exercise

Move the 2D Euler loop into the animation callback. Advance several steps per frame, reapply the Neumann boundaries, and update the image.

```python
import matplotlib.animation as animation
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

steps_per_frame = 200

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
im = ax.imshow(uv[1], origin="lower", extent=[0, length_y, 0, length_x], vmin=1, vmax=3.5)


def update_frame(_):
    # TODO: advance uv by steps_per_frame Euler steps
    # TODO: reapply Neumann boundary conditions after each step
    im.set_array(uv[1])
    return (im,)


ani = animation.FuncAnimation(fig, update_frame, interval=1, blit=True)
plt.show()
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution

`global` is needed because the callback reassigns `uv`. Inside a wrapping function, use `nonlocal` instead.

```python
def update_frame(_):
    global uv
    for _ in range(steps_per_frame):
        uv = uv + dt * gierer_meinhardt_pde_2d(0, uv, d=30, dx=dx)
        uv = apply_boundary_conditions(uv, bc="neumann")
    im.set_array(uv[1])
    return (im,)
```
:::
